## Materials and Methods

## COMSOL simulation

There are several empirical studies on inertial microfluidic separation devices. However; to our knowledge, no group has focused on the computational simulation of these devices. In this study, simulation was conducted based on the data from a past empirical work called the Contraction Expansion Array (CEA) as a reference (Figure   IA) to verify the simulations 16 The CEA is straight channel with six contraction regions, two inlets, and two outlets. The dimensions of the CEA are in table 1 The general objective in this part is to modify the con figuration of the to improve the separation efficiency. From it is known that both Dean force and inertial lift force are affected by the geometry of the channel. Hence; manipulating the channel was elaborated by manipulating its geometry with a software The software COMSOL Multiphysics 5.2@ was used to simulate the 3D module of the particles flowing in the CEA\_ Primary   assumptions were about   rigid spherical particles diffused in a laminar of a liquid with the characteristics of water. Laminar flow and par ticle tracing physics are the physics used in COMSOL system theory , Drag geometry flow environment. Dean drag force equation is assumed to follow stokes equation all over the device and the inertial lift force term was inserted manually , different for contractions and expansions regions. Then;, the effect ofthe angle between two inlets, the depth of the channel, the shape of expansion arrays and the ratio between the two inlet flow rates with simulation were evaluated. Fig ure IB shows the properties of the optimized CEA according to simulation results. The optimized device is called the simulation-modified CEA smCEA) drag

## Fabrication of the design

The devices were prepared by soft lithogra phy protocol 25 In this method, molds of the smCEA were prepared with SU-8 photoresist on a glass substrate following the conventional  photolithography  process Then; Poly Di-methyl Siloxane (PDMS) and its curing agent (Sylgard 184; Dow Corning, MI) in a ratio of 10:1 were poured on stamps and cured in a 6Soven overnight. The  PDMS layer bonded to a glass slide by treating both surfaces with an air-plasma treatment process in low pressure (500 mTorr) chamber (Figure 2). The plasma treatment process made PDMS hydrophilic.

The smCEA was fabricated according to the simula tion outcome. The smCEA, similar to the CEA, has two inlets for a flow containing cells (particle fluid) and particle-less fluid with the same physical charac

## Sample preparation

Two approaches in the preparation of the particle fluid were used while the focusing fluid was the same during the experiments . PBS was used as the focusing fluid. For the first set of experiment, a combination of fixed mouse fibroblast cell line (L929) (10-15 um in di ameter) and breast cancer cell line (MCF7) (18-25 um in diameter)   with predefined density was suspended in PBS to form the particle fluid. For the second set of ex periment; first, the whole blood was diluted 100 times with PBS, and then suspension of MCF7 fixed cells was spiked into the blood. Whole blood was obtained from Iranian Blood Transfusion Organization (IBTO)
